chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halbi, from Abdul Hameed al-Ta'i who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'We are walkers, so what should we do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the owners of the rides, they used to pray the morning prayer in Mina, and as for you, go until you pray in the road.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الرِّحَالِ: Owners of the rides/camels, referring to those traveling by animal.
key_terms.فِي الطَّرِيقِ: In the road, referring to the route between Mina and Arafat.
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj.

ai.seo_question: When should pilgrims walking to Arafat perform their morning prayer during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *rukhas* (concessions) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam differentiates ritual obligations based on the pilgrim's physical exertion and mode of travel. It underscores the practical flexibility granted to those walking to Arafat, allowing them to delay Fajr until they reach the road, thereby prioritizing ease over rigid timing during the critical journey.
